key_insight: A reasoning-enabled LLM can significantly improve speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas by using broader narrative context, not just local utterance cues. The paper also introduces a large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, to train and evaluate this capability at scale.
problem_solved: The paper tackles speaker recognition in long TV dramas, where it is difficult to correctly assign each spoken line to the right character because of many characters, long story arcs, and overlapping dialogue context.
method: Builds DramaSR-532K, a benchmark with 532K annotated dialogue lines from 900+ unique characters.
Uses a reasoning-focused LLM to leverage dialogue context and storyline information for speaker attribution.
Evaluates speaker recognition in long-form drama settings, where memory, context tracking, and character relations matter more than isolated speech cues.
impact: This work shows that reasoning-centric LLMs can help solve real multimedia understanding tasks that require long-context inference. For practitioners, it suggests a path toward more accurate character-level understanding in entertainment analytics, media indexing, and narrative-aware AI systems.

paper_title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
paper_authors: Yuxuan Li, Lingxi Xie, Xinyue Huo, Jihao Qiu, Jiacheng Shao
